title: Nature defended
sub: Eleven defenses of species, land, forests and oceans, and where they fall short
lede: Protected areas, a whaling ban, the High Seas Treaty, forest monitoring, restoration law and the money behind them. Each entry says what exists, what the evidence shows it has done and how solid that evidence is. A section near the end lists where the defenses are thinning.
asof: Figures current to 13 October 2026. The framework's global review opens on 19 October, so its verdict is not yet in.

p: The framework has 23 global targets, including the aim of protecting at least 30 percent of land and ocean by 2030. By the August 2026 meetings in Nairobi, 172 Parties, almost 90 percent, had submitted national targets, and 130 had submitted national reports. The first global review of progress is due at COP17, 19 to 30 October 2026, in Yerevan.
How solid From the Convention's own press releases. The 2022 adoption date is general knowledge. The review at COP17 had not happened when I wrote this.

kv.v: The Executive Secretary told the Nairobi meeting that fewer than half of aligned national targets assessed by Parties are currently on track.
Mobilizing biodiversity finance, reforming harmful subsidies, addressing business impacts and dependencies, and shifting toward sustainable consumption.

items.solid: How solid From the Convention's own press releases. The 2022 adoption date is general knowledge. The review at COP17 had not happened when I wrote this.

p: The Protected Planet Report 2024 puts coverage at 17.6 percent of land and inland waters and 8.4 percent of ocean and coastal areas. Since 2020, 629,000 square kilometres of land and 1.77 million square kilometres of sea have been added. 51 countries and territories exceed 30 percent on land, and 31 exceed it at sea.
How solid From the report's executive summary, a UN-backed dataset of official submissions. Coverage is counted by area, so it does not show whether protection is enforced.

kv.v: Another 16.7 million square kilometres (12.4 percent) of land and 78.3 million (21.6 percent) of sea.

Only 8.52 percent of land is both protected and connected. Only 5.7 percent of the ocean is in marine protected areas that are implemented or actively managed, and 2.8 percent is fully or highly protected.
Over two-thirds of key biodiversity areas are partially or fully covered, and the remaining 32 percent lie entirely outside protected areas.

items.solid: How solid From the report's executive summary, a UN-backed dataset of official submissions. Coverage is counted by area, so it does not show whether protection is enforced.

p: The Agreement on Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction passed 60 ratifications on 20 September 2025, with Sierra Leone and Morocco the last two to deposit. It entered into force on 17 January 2026. Palau was the first to ratify, on 22 January 2024.
How solid IUCN's announcement. I found no marine protected area yet created under the treaty, and the page does not give the share of ocean the treaty covers.

kv.v: Marine protected areas beyond national jurisdiction, environmental impact assessments, and rules on access to and benefit sharing from marine genetic resources.

items.solid: How solid IUCN's announcement. I found no marine protected area yet created under the treaty, and the page does not give the share of ocean the treaty covers.

items.h3: Whaling ban and the humpback whale
p: Commercial whaling was curbed and then banned in 1986. Humpbacks in the western South Atlantic fell to a low of 440 in 1958, from about 27,000 before hunting. A 2019 study estimates about 25,000 now, roughly 93 percent of the pre-hunt level.
How solid One population of one species, reported by Science News. Other whale populations recovered less, and the ban is only one factor.

kv.v: Zerbini and colleagues, Royal Society Open Science, published online 16 October 2019.

items.solid: How solid One population of one species, reported by Science News. Other whale populations recovered less, and the ban is only one factor.

p: Bolam and colleagues estimate that conservation action prevented at least 28 bird and mammal extinctions since 1993: 21 to 32 birds and 7 to 16 mammals. They drew on 137 experts.
How solid The figures are estimates of what would have happened without conservation, not counts. The study covers birds and mammals only.

kv.v: In the same period 15 bird and mammal species went extinct or are strongly suspected to have done so. The vaquita is still declining quickly.

items.solid: How solid The figures are estimates of what would have happened without conservation, not counts. The study covers birds and mammals only.

p: Brazil's DETER system recorded 2,874.38 square kilometres of deforestation alerts from August 2025 to July 2026, down from 4,495 in the previous period. That is the lowest since the series began in 2016 and 55.6 percent below the average of the last ten cycles.

How solid A report in Agência Brasil of figures from the national space research institute. The article says the fall was 36.87 percent, but the two areas it gives imply about 36.06 percent, and it does not explain the gap. Alerts are not the same as the annual official count.
items.solid: How solid A report in Agência Brasil of figures from the national space research institute. The article says the fall was 36.87 percent, but the two areas it gives imply about 36.06 percent, and it does not explain the gap. Alerts are not the same as the annual official count.

p: The law took effect on 18 August 2024. Member States must have restoration measures in place on at least 20 percent of the EU's land and 20 percent of its sea by 2030, and for all ecosystems that need restoration by 2050.
How solid From the European Commission's announcement. I did not check whether Member States met the 2026 deadline for draft plans.

kv.v: Draft national restoration plans are due two years after entry into force, so about August 2026, with reviews by 2032 and 2042.
The law aims to restore at least 25,000 kilometres of rivers by 2030.

items.solid: How solid From the European Commission's announcement. I did not check whether Member States met the 2026 deadline for draft plans.

items.h3: Ozone layer and the Montreal Protocol
p: The phase-out covers nearly 99 percent of banned ozone-depleting substances. If current policies stay, the ozone layer is expected to return to 1980 levels by about 2066 over the Antarctic, 2045 over the Arctic and 2040 elsewhere. In the 2026 Planetary Health Check, stratospheric ozone is one of two boundaries that are not transgressed.
How solid The WMO page and a summary of the 2026 check. The 1987 date is general knowledge. Ozone and aerosols are the two boundaries that have improved over the last decade.
items.solid: How solid The WMO page and a summary of the 2026 check. The 1987 date is general knowledge. Ozone and aerosols are the two boundaries that have improved over the last decade.

p: Wild catch has stayed in a band of 86 to 94 million tonnes since the late 1980s, about 92 million tonnes in 2024, while farmed aquatic animal production passed 100 million tonnes. 62.4 percent of assessed stocks are fished sustainably.
How solid FAO's 2026 report through Mongabay. A steady catch can reflect management or limits on stocks, and the report's stock count changed from about 500 to 2,665 between editions.

kv.v: The sustainable share fell 2.1 points from the 2024 report.

items.solid: How solid FAO's 2026 report through Mongabay. A steady catch can reflect management or limits on stocks, and the report's stock count changed from about 500 to 2,665 between editions.

p: At the International Seabed Authority's two-week Council session reported on 20 March 2026, no mining was approved. The Mining Code, the rulebook needed before commercial extraction, remains unfinished. 40 countries back a moratorium.
How solid A report in Oceanographic Magazine. I did not find the outcome of the July meeting, so this describes the position in March.

kv.v: Concern about unilateral mining outside the Authority, centred on a Nauru-linked subsidiary of The Metals Company. A report on it was due at the July meeting.

items.solid: How solid A report in Oceanographic Magazine. I did not find the outcome of the July meeting, so this describes the position in March.

p: International finance to developing countries was $29.8 billion in 2023 for biodiversity-related spending and $16.8 billion for biodiversity-specific spending, against a target of $20 billion a year by 2025. The 2030 target is $30 billion a year.
How solid From a UK government finance dashboard. The page gives no current total for the $200 billion target or for subsidies, so I cannot say how close either is.

kv.v: $200 billion a year from all sources by 2030, and $500 billion of harmful subsidies reduced or reformed.
A $700 billion annual biodiversity funding gap by 2030.
$220 billion of total annual flows in 2023, up 11 percent on 2022, of which $23.4 billion was private.

items.solid: How solid From a UK government finance dashboard. The page gives no current total for the $200 billion target or for subsidies, so I cannot say how close either is.

patterns.h3: Defenses work best on a single, countable cause
p: The whaling ban, the ozone chemicals and the Amazon alerts each target one act that can be monitored. The recoveries in this chapter are of that kind.
The 30 percent targets stand against 17.6 and 8.4 percent coverage and much smaller shares that are managed or strictly protected.

patterns.h3: Diffuse drivers have no comparable instrument
p: Land-use change, consumption, plastic and ocean heat are spread across many actors. For these the entries describe frameworks and negotiations, and I found no measured turnaround.

The humpback population reached about 93 percent of its pre-hunt size roughly 33 years after the ban, and the same studies show other species still falling. Conservation prevented at least 28 extinctions while 15 others occurred.

limits: The list is my selection. Eleven entries cannot cover the many local and national defenses, and I did not cover freshwater protection, soil, invasive species control or national endangered species laws.
Cause is hard to show. A rise in a population or fall in deforestation may reflect enforcement, prices, weather or all three, and the sources say so in only some cases.
Several items are early. The framework's global review, the July seabed meeting and the national restoration plans were still pending or unchecked when I wrote this.
Coverage counts area, not outcome. A protected area that is not managed is counted in the 17.6 and 8.4 percent.
Most figures reached me through summaries, so they need checking against the original reports before use.

footer: Two statements are general knowledge and were not tied to a fetched source: that the Global Biodiversity Framework was adopted in 2022 and that the Montreal Protocol dates from 1987. The 1.6 percent and 68 percent bars are my arithmetic, as is the gap I noted between the Amazon alert percentages. The observations under “What the defenses have in common” are my reading. I read the plastics-treaty session date as 2026 from the page's retrieval date, which the page does not state outright.
